interpretation: A2 agreement with recorded masked V14 argmax is compared on identical known development features and masks to the four earlier RL endpoints. Lower agreement and higher teacher regret establish a change in learned preferences on this fixed data distribution.
Raw Q-MSE decomposes into centered action-value mismatch and squared per-row legal mean shift. A common value shift changes neither masked argmax nor regret; these components must not be conflated.

These rows are excluded from supervised learning and teacher calibration, but remain development data (five seeds, both sides, two collector distributions), not a fresh performance test. Correlated rows are not independent games.

Teacher Q values are scores on recorded feature vectors; recorded collector final actions/overrides belong to the collector and are identical across evaluated model roles. They are not final actions of these evaluated RL models or teacher.

Reduced teacher agreement is not proof that forgetting caused losses: teacher need not be optimal; useful RL adaptation can disagree; final rule overrides, later state distributions, and win outcomes are not reconstructed. Fresh paired intervention results are required to assess the fixed weak anchor.
